title: This Volcano Burns With Blue Flames 16 Feet High

scenes.text: This volcano burns with blue fire sixteen feet high.
It's Kawah Ijen in Indonesia, and the blue isn't lava.
It's sulfur gas, escaping from cracks at over one thousand degrees Fahrenheit.
The gas ignites the moment it hits the air, and it keeps burning as liquid sulfur runs downhill.
You can only see it at night. In daylight, the glow disappears.
A sixteen-foot wall of blue fire.

description:
Kawah Ijen volcano in Indonesia glows with electric blue flames up to 16 feet high.
The blue is burning sulfur gas, escaping at up to 1,112 degrees Fahrenheit, and it is only visible at night.
Would you hike up to see it?
first_comment: Bonus: the flames look blue but the real fire is red-orange hot at 600 C. Would you hike a volcano at midnight to see it?
